analysis.description: The paper introduces Preferential Temporal Difference (Preferential TD or PTD) learning, a novel algorithm that emphasizes the importance of a state in TD updates using a state-dependent preference function. The method converges with linear function approximation and shows promising empirical results compared to other TD-style methods.

type.justification: The paper provides theoretical analysis and proofs of convergence for the proposed algorithm (Preferential TD), though empirical behavior is also illustrated.
type.quote: We prove that our approach converges with linear function approximation and illustrate its desirable empirical behaviour compared to other TD-style methods.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on temporal-difference learning methods, which are a core component of reinforcement learning.
name.quote: Temporal-Difference (TD) learning is a general and very useful tool for estimating the value function of a given policy, which in turn is required to find good policies.
